explanation: On strong heating, calcium carbonate decomposes into calcium oxide (quicklime) and carbon dioxide gas.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: A white solid, calcium carbonate (limestone, marble chips, or chalk).
beaker_view.final_appearance: Still a white solid (calcium oxide), but reduced in mass as gas has escaped.

thermal.visual_cue: Needs strong, sustained heating to decompose at all.

beaker_view.observation: There's no obvious colour change in the solid itself — the clearest sign this reacted is the gas given off, which turns lime water milky when passed through it.
